correctness.rationale: The local theorem holds in the stated sum-of-vertex metric. At the orthogonal pentagon pair, each of the 25 edge-pair tetrahedra has a strict supporting gap to the six remaining vertices, and the origin is interior; these simplex facets persist and their consistently oriented determinants give 24 times the volume. The first variation vanishes by the cyclic cancellation of angular differences, with the mixed wedge contributions starting at second order. In the second variation, the in-plane area loses s/4 times the angular difference energy and s/2 times the squared cross velocities. Only first-harmonic cross velocities contribute linearly to the mixed bivectors. For their matrix parts M,N the mixed pairing is the quadratic term of the block determinant of [[I,tN],[tM,I]], namely -tr(MN) times the squared base area; pairing with the radial losses yields the stated squared norm of M+N^T. The five-cycle Laplacian and the splitting N=±M^T, with matrix metric factor 5/2, give all 30 eigenvalues with six precisely rotational zeros. Normal displacement from a compact smooth orbit has chordal distance equal to its length to first order, so Taylor's factor 1/2 gives the sharp 25/192 and the first angular mode realizes it. The externally cited global maximum is antecedent, not reproved here.
